readings: Match budget lines to their events (drop budget lines with no matching event) and, for each event name, compute the average budgeted `amount`, ignoring missing amounts. Call the plain average of these per-event-name averages (each name counting once) the overall average, and keep only the event names whose average is above it. For each kept event name, show the event name, its average budgeted amount, its average minus the overall average, and its average divided by the average of the per-event-name averages taken over only the kept above-average event names (not the overall average). Do not round.
queries:
WITH per_name AS (
    SELECT e.event_name AS event_name, AVG(b.amount) AS avg_amount
    FROM budget b
    JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
    GROUP BY e.event_name
),
overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS overall_avg FROM per_name
),
kept AS (
    SELECT p.event_name, p.avg_amount
    FROM per_name p, overall o
    WHERE p.avg_amount > o.overall_avg
),
kept_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS kept_avg FROM kept
)
SELECT k.event_name,
       k.avg_amount,
       k.avg_amount - o.overall_avg AS diff_from_overall,
       k.avg_amount / ka.kept_avg AS ratio_to_kept_avg
FROM kept k, overall o, kept_avg ka;
